title: Acceptance implies proximity to the property
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty domain, let $\beta$ be a finite alphabet, and let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester with a finite seed space and acceptance probability $\Pr[T\text{ accepts }f]$ on each function $f:\Omega\to\beta$. Let $P$ be a property of such functions and let $\mathrm{rate}\in\mathbb R$. Assume $\mathrm{rate}>0$, every function in $P$ is accepted with probability $1$, and for each $\delta\in[0,1]$ every function whose relative Hamming distance from every function in $P$ exceeds $\delta$ has rejection probability greater than $\mathrm{rate}\,\delta$. If $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ and $f:\Omega\to\beta$ is accepted with probability at least $1-\mathrm{rate}\,\varepsilon$, then there exists a function $g\in P$ whose relative Hamming distance from $f$ is at most $\varepsilon$.
